"Create a playable 2D dark fantasy turn-based battle game.

The game is a 1v1 battle between a player and an AI opponent.

Each character has HP, attack power and speed.

COMBAT:

- Both players have independent timers.
- Each action window lasts 10 seconds.
- Turns are asynchronous, not alternating.
- Speed determines how frequently a character gets another turn, NOT who acts first.
- Each turn allows one combat play.
- Players can move on a grid, attack or switch characters.

SPEED MECHANIC:
After performing a play, the remaining wait time until the next turn is reduced by a percentage based on speed.
This reduction happens immediately, does not stack and applies only once per turn.

Include three selectable character types:

1. Insatiability: loses speed to gain attack power.
2. Scarcity: gains stronger bonuses on the next turn when acting with more time remaining.
3. Cannibalism: sacrifices its own HP or damages enemies to trigger special effects.

Use simple controls, visible timers, health bars and clear combat feedback.

Use a dark fantasy pixel art aesthetic.

Make it genuinely playable. Focus on testing the combat mechanics, not story, graphics or complex progression.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D dark-fantasy turn-based battle game in the existing project.

## Requirements
- 1v1 player-versus-AI battle with independent 10-second action windows; turns are asynchronous, and speed changes the next-turn wait, not action order.
- One play per turn: grid movement, attack, or character switch. Speed reduction applies immediately, once per turn, without stacking.
- Include Insatiability, Scarcity, and Cannibalism character types; show timers, health bars, and clear combat feedback.
- Simple controls, pixel-art-inspired dark fantasy aesthetic; prioritize playable combat mechanics over story or progression.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone `index.html` with inline CSS and JavaScript, no build tools or package dependencies.
- Player controls three roster characters, with one active at a time; AI also has three characters.
- Assumed movement consumes a play, attacks are orthogonal Manhattan-range attacks, and AI runs on its own independent clock.
